questions.stem: A family from Perth spends a week snorkelling on the Great Barrier Reef. This is an example of:
options: international tourism
business tourism
outbound tourism
domestic tourism
questions.explanation: Domestic tourism is travel within your own country, so a trip from Western Australia to Queensland counts. International tourism involves crossing a national border, and business tourism is travel for work.

questions.stem: Which is a key benefit of tourism businesses owned and led by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples?
options: They replace all government funding for health and education in communities
They create jobs on Country and let communities share culture on their own terms
They allow visitors to enter any sacred site they wish to see without asking
They remove any need to ask permission before photographing ceremonies or people
questions.explanation: First Nations-led tourism brings income and jobs to communities, supports keeping culture strong and lets Traditional Owners decide what is shared and how. Visitors learn directly from the people whose Country it is.

questions.stem: At a national park, signs placed at the request of the Traditional Owners ask visitors not to photograph a sacred site. What should a culturally respectful visitor do?
options: Photograph it, as long as the photos are for personal use only
Photograph it, as long as no people appear anywhere in the picture
Photograph it, but avoid posting the picture on social media
Not photograph it, and follow the Traditional Owners' guidance
questions.explanation: Some sites have deep cultural significance, and the Traditional Owners have asked that they not be photographed at all. Respecting that request applies whatever the photos would be used for.

options: A prepaid card used to pay for purchases in foreign currencies while travelling
Permission from another country to enter or stay there for a set purpose and time
A document issued by the Australian Government proving your identity and citizenship
An insurance policy that covers medical costs and lost luggage while overseas
questions.explanation: A visa is issued by the country you are visiting and sets out why and for how long you may stay. Your passport, issued by Australia, proves who you are and that you are an Australian citizen.

questions.stem: Before booking an overseas trip, why should Mia check when her passport expires?
options: An expired passport can still be used as long as a visa is attached to it
Airlines renew passengers' passports at check-in for a small extra fee
Many countries require a passport to be valid for months beyond the date of travel
Every Australian passport must be renewed before each new overseas trip can be booked
questions.explanation: Many countries refuse entry, and airlines may refuse boarding, if a passport is close to expiring, often within six months. Renewing takes time, so the expiry date should be checked before anything is booked.

questions.stem: Why is travel insurance strongly recommended for overseas trips?
options: The Australian embassy pays travellers' medical bills only if they have insurance
Medicare generally does not cover treatment overseas, and medical bills there can be huge
Medicare covers all overseas medical costs, but insurance is still needed for lost luggage
Airlines are not allowed to sell tickets to travellers who have no travel insurance
questions.explanation: Apart from limited agreements with some countries, Medicare does not pay for treatment overseas, and hospital care or an emergency flight home can cost tens of thousands of dollars. The Australian Government will not pay these bills for travellers.

questions.stem: Which list gives the Australian Government's Smartraveller advice levels in order, from lowest to highest risk?
options: Reconsider your need to travel; exercise normal safety precautions; exercise a high degree of caution; do not travel
Exercise normal safety precautions; exercise a high degree of caution; reconsider your need to travel; do not travel
Exercise a high degree of caution; exercise normal safety precautions; do not travel; reconsider your need to travel
Exercise normal safety precautions; reconsider your need to travel; exercise a high degree of caution; do not travel
questions.explanation: Smartraveller, run by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, uses four levels, from normal precautions up to do not travel. Travellers should check the advice before booking and again before leaving, because levels change and some insurance policies do not cover travel to the highest-risk places.

questions.stem: Ella budgets for a hotel in Japan costing 15,000 yen a night when $1 (Australian) buys 100 yen. Before she pays, the Australian dollar falls so that $1 buys only 90 yen. What happens to the cost of a night?
options: It falls to about $135
It stays at $150, because the price is in yen
It rises to about $1,667
It rises to about $167
questions.explanation: At 100 yen per dollar the room costs 15,000 ÷ 100 = $150; at 90 yen it costs 15,000 ÷ 90 ≈ $167. A weaker Australian dollar buys fewer yen, so overseas prices cost more in Australian dollars, even though the yen price has not changed.

questions.stem: Which is a sensible way to manage money while travelling overseas?
options: Carry two payment methods, keep them apart, and know how to cancel a lost card
Keep all your cash and cards together in one wallet so they are always easy to find
Always choose to be charged in Australian dollars at overseas shops and ATMs
Never tell your bank you are going overseas, so your card is not blocked
questions.explanation: If one card is lost or stolen, a second kept elsewhere means you can still pay, and quick cancellation limits losses. Choosing to pay in Australian dollars overseas usually means a poor exchange rate set by the shop or ATM, and banks often ask to be told about travel plans.

questions.stem: An Australian traveller is arrested overseas for carrying a medicine that is legal in Australia but banned in that country. Which statement is correct?
options: Local laws and penalties apply to them, even if they are harsher than Australia's
Australian law applies to them, because they are travelling on an Australian passport
The Australian embassy can order the local police to release them straight away
Tourists are exempt from local drug laws as long as they declare it at customs
questions.explanation: Travellers are bound by the laws of the country they are in, and penalties for drug offences in some countries are very severe. Before travelling, check whether your medicines are allowed and carry a doctor's letter.

questions.stem: Which of these can Australian consular officials do for a traveller in trouble overseas?
options: Pay their legal fees, hospital bills or fines out of government funds
Get them released from prison, even if a local court has convicted them
Overturn a local court's decision if it seems unfair to Australians
Contact their family, give a list of local lawyers and visit them if detained
questions.explanation: Consular staff can offer practical help and check on the welfare of Australians who are arrested, but they cannot interfere in another country's legal system or pay a traveller's bills. That limit is why insurance and obeying local laws matter so much.

questions.stem: Why is Australia's main diplomatic office in London called a high commission rather than an embassy?
options: It handles only trade matters, so it does not help Australian travellers
It is bigger than an embassy and has authority over every Australian consulate
The United Kingdom is not an independent country, so it cannot host an embassy
Australia and the United Kingdom are both members of the Commonwealth
questions.explanation: Between Commonwealth countries the main diplomatic mission is called a high commission; elsewhere it is an embassy. Both do the same job, and consulates are smaller offices in other cities that also help travellers.

questions.stem: When international tourists spend money in Australia on hotels, tours and meals, how is this counted in Australia's trade figures?
options: As a goods import
As a goods export
As a services import
As a services export
questions.explanation: Foreign visitors are buying Australian services with money earned overseas, so their spending counts as a services export, just like international students' fees. Australians spending money on holidays overseas count as a services import.

questions.stem: What is one advantage of booking a complex overseas trip through a travel agent rather than booking everything online yourself?
options: Expert advice, and help to rearrange bookings if plans are disrupted
Travel agents are not allowed to charge any fees for their booking services
Bookings made through an agent do not need passports or visas
Agents guarantee that flights they book will never be cancelled
questions.explanation: A travel agent can package flights, accommodation and tours and help when things go wrong, though they may charge fees. Booking online yourself can be cheaper and more flexible but leaves you to sort out problems alone.
